subject: AirSeal: Signed Bundle Rotation & Emergency Fallback for Isolated Kiosk Fleet
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Ops Team (Ironclad Logistics) <ops@ironcladlogistics.com>, Alan Brooks <alan.brooks@ironcladlogistics.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 4 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: AirSeal: Signed Bundle Rotation & Emergency Fallback for Isolated Kiosk Fleet

Hi Alan / Ironclad ops team —

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. As discussed, we need a tight, auditable process for rotating signed images to your offline kiosk fleet and a clear emergency fallback path if an activation fails on-site. This thread captures the recommended flow and a few open questions before we lock the SOP.

High level proposal (summary):
- Redwood produces signed bundles (GPG detached + SHA256 manifest) per customer release. The signature is generated by our HSM-backed build service and a corresponding notarization record is pushed to the private control plane.
- Ironclad receives the signed bundle files via secure courier or hand-delivered USB. Each bundle includes: image tarball, manifest.json (with checksums + epoch), signature (.sig), and an acceptance nonce.
- On-site operator uses the acceptance checklist (attached) to verify checksums and signature using the offline verify tool, then stages into the kiosk staging partition.
- Activation window: operator triggers a signed activation token exchange with the kiosk agent. The agent validates the bundle signature against the embedded public key and the nonce; on success it swaps partitions and writes an activation log (signed locally).
- Emergency fallback: kiosks keep the previous signed image in a preserved partition. If health checks fail within the grace window (10 minutes + smoke tests), the kiosk runs a signed rollback script that reverts to the prior partition and emits a rollback-forensics tar to the acceptance folder.

Open questions we should confirm:
1) Ironclad acceptance: do you prefer courier-delivered sealed USB (we provide tamper tags) or bonded driver handoff?
2) Nonce exchange: should the acceptance nonce be single-use per kiosk or per batch?
3) Audit ingestion: we will provide a signed activation log bundle. Do you want these sent back on courier or uploaded later via a secure ingress path at the depot?

Attachments: operator-handback-checklist.xlsx (checklist + operator signature line), kiosk-network-diagram.png (shows the isolated LAN layout), airseal_signed_bundle_v1.tar.sig (signature stub).

Next step: can Ironclad confirm preferred physical delivery and whether you can run the offline verify tool (we can provide a signed binary) during your operator on-boarding next Wed (9/8)?

Thanks —

Marissa Cole
Head of Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

From: Alan Brooks <alan.brooks@ironcladlogistics.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ops Team (Ironclad Logistics) <ops@ironcladlogistics.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Sep 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: AirSeal: Signed Bundle Rotation & Emergency Fallback for Isolated Kiosk Fleet

Marissa —

Thanks for the summary. Quick answers from ops:
- Delivery: bonded driver handoff is our default for high-priority rollouts; courier-sealed USB for smaller updates. We can accept tamper tags (please include serial and tamper ID).
- Nonce: single-use per kiosk gives us the strongest protection against replay but increases logistics complexity. We're leaning single-use per kiosk for critical security patches and batch nonces for routine deltas.
- Audit ingestion: for now, courier return of signed activation logs is preferred. Our depots have the paper chain-of-custody and we ingest artifacts when they return to the depot.

We can run the offline verify tool during the operator onboarding on Wed 9/8 at the North Depot; please provide the binary and a short checklist.

Alan
Operations Lead
Ironclad Logistics
ops@ironcladlogistics.com

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Alan Brooks <alan.brooks@ironcladlogistics.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 8 Sep 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: AirSeal: Signed Bundle Rotation & Emergency Fallback for Isolated Kiosk Fleet

Alan / team —

Great, thanks for confirming delivery preferences. A few engineering clarifications from our side before the 9/8 onboarding:

1) Signature verification: our offline verifier supports both OpenPGP detached signatures and PKCS7; for the kiosks we'll embed the Redwood public verification key in the agent and ship a short chain-of-trust file that lists the HSM key ID + revocation epoch. The operator-run verify tool will print a three-line acceptance summary (manifest checksum OK / signature OK / nonce OK).

2) Nonce handling: implementing single-use nonce per kiosk requires including per-kiosk nonce values in the manifest. That means the build pipeline needs to accept a per-kiosk identifier at bundle generation. If this is acceptable to Ironclad we can add that to the build flow; otherwise we will default to batch nonces with per-kiosk runtime freshness checks (timestamp + operator PIN).

3) Rollback forensic: the kiosk will collect the following on rollback: preserved journal (systemd logs), agent debug snapshot, and the failed activation tarball. The acceptance checklist asks operators to physically note any peripheral failures (power/nic/cables). We will sign the forensic tar with a local key and attach to the activation record.

Action items for onboarding 9/8:
- Redwood: provide signed offline verifier binary (sha256: a1b2...f3), operator-handback-checklist.xlsx, and the first sample signed bundle for test.
- Ironclad: provide a test kiosk image (kiosk-id 0001) and a depot operator for hands-on verification.

I'll be on the call to run through the verify flow.

Jonas
Sr. SRE, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Date: Thu, 9 Sep 2026 12:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: AirSeal: Signed Bundle Rotation & Emergency Fallback for Isolated Kiosk Fleet

Folks —

Couple of compliance notes from security:
- All bundles must include a revocation field in manifest.json and a build epoch timestamp. If Ironclad finds a tamper tag mismatch we need a revocation workflow that prevents any subsequent activations until a new bundle is issued.
- For the acceptance logs we require operator identity confirmation: operator badge ID + printed signature line. The operator-handback-checklist.xlsx includes that field.
- We should avoid shipping private keys on any media. Verification keys only. The rollback diagnostic tar will be encrypted with a depot public key so courier returns remain confidential.

Kimberly
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Date: Thu, 9 Sep 2026 16:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: AirSeal: Signed Bundle Rotation & Emergency Fallback for Isolated Kiosk Fleet

Thanks all —

Summary / decisions captured: 
- Delivery: Ironclad will use bonded driver handoff for the initial rollout; tamper-tag serials required.
- Nonce policy: single-use per kiosk for critical patches; batch nonces for routine deltas. Redwood will extend the build pipeline to accept per-kiosk IDs (Jonas to coordinate).
- Audit logs: courier return for now; we will revisit secure depot upload in Q4.
- Compliance: include revocation field + epoch; rollback tars encrypted with depot public key; operator badge ID required on the checklist.

Action items: 
- Jonas: update build pipeline to accept per-kiosk nonce IDs and share timestamped sample bundle by EOD 9/10.
- Marissa: send signed offline verifier binary and operator-handback-checklist bundle to Alan (attached).
- Ironclad (Alan): confirm bonded driver pickup slot for the first sealed bundle (target window: 9/14 - 9/16).

I'll circulate a one-page SOP after 9/8 onboarding and attach final checklists + courier tags. If anyone needs to escalate before then, please ping me.

Best —

Marissa Cole
Head of Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

Attachments: airseal_signed_bundle_v1.tar.sig; operator-handback-checklist.xlsx; kiosk-network-diagram.png
